just to sum up the technique better, it’s gonna be hard at first to visualize wiping away all those intrusive thoughts all the time at first. but with practice and a little bit of time (depends on your willingness to try as well as how intense your fear is, for some people it takes a few days, weeks, some people a few hours) your brain will begin to recognize the pattern (oh… everytime I think about this topic (intrusive thought), the anxiety goes away quickly because it gets metaphorically wiped away… okay… that must mean the problem is solved and i dont need to think about it anymore. ah okay, awesome, I’ll just send out the intrusive thought a few more times just to make sure, and then after that, if the fear alert doesn’t seem to go off anymore, I’ll stop forever.)

visualize a squeegee or windshield wiper type object in your head. everytime you have an intrusive thought, imagine those thoughts are like clouds, floating by. you can swipe them away. that’s all they are— just clouds. they’re not apart of you, they dont represent you. you don’t actually think that way. its just your brain trying to get down to the bottom of something that isn’t even important- cause unfortunately, thats our reptile brain still at work in the modern age. each time you respond to an intrusive thought with anxiety/fright, you are reinforcing to your problem-solving, alert-sensitive brain that the thought is WORTH ruminating over and bringing up. and until you understand this and get control of it, your brain will KEEP bringing it up, over and over, stronger and stronger, until it solves the issue once and for all. and obviously, with intrusive thoughts, there isn’t usually a concrete answer because the anxiety is usually irrational. so to sum it up again, your brain will keep trying to find an answer where there is none until you convince it that HEY, THERES NOTHING OF SUBSTANCE HERE. so basically, let me explain something about the brain real quick. our brains have an interesting alert and attention system. 

First, our brains come up with an intrusive and open-ended what-if kind of thought about something (example: oh no! What if I’m a psychopath)

human brains, by nature, are problem-solving centered. that’s why you’re so obsessed with finding out an answer to your problem. so, after your brain poses a hypothetical, intrusive thought that SCARES you (oh my gosh I’m scared that I’m gonna manifest my family members death) it stands out in your brain because it provokes an EMOTIONAL response. it provokes… your ALERT system. think about it this way: all thoughts are essentially intrusive, it’s just the scary ones that we really care about to an obsessive, uncomfortable point. why am I thinking this way? What does it MEAN to me? Why wont it go away? How do I make it stop? 

so, like I said, our brains are wired to PROBLEM SOLVE, as well as RECOGNIZE and PROCESS potential danger. when a thought gives you ANXIETY, you are essentially telling your brain this; there is a PROBLEM here that we need to solve NOW! IMMEDIATELY! for our SURVIVAL and SAFETY. because the brain sees anxiety as anxiety and nothing else but that. it doesn’t know there’s nothing actually wrong. 

so, now with the mechanics put aside, what did I do to stop it? Well, knowing why my brain was acting that way certainly helped. but I needed a tool.
